Domain Reasoning: Core entities: Board (4x4 grid of ints), Game (stateful orchestrator of board, score, RNG), Direction (enum-like for LEFT, RIGHT, UP, DOWN), GameStatus (RUNNING, WON, LOST).
Movement rules: on a move, lines/columns shift toward the move direction, compacting zeros, merging equal adjacent tiles exactly once per move, from the direction of movement.
Single-merge-per-move rule: a tile resulting from a merge cannot merge again in the same move.
Scoring: the sum of merged values in a move is added to the total score.
Deterministic tile spawning: after a successful move (board changes), spawn exactly one new tile (value 2 with high probability, 4 with low), using a seeded RNG for reproducibility.
Win/Loss: win when a tile reaches 2048; lose when no moves are possible. GameStatus updates accordingly.
Reset: reset(seed?) initializes the board with two tiles placed deterministically from the RNG seeded during Game construction.

Canonical pure line logic: move_line_left(line: list[int]) -> tuple[list[int], int] must strictly follow: values = [v for v in line if v != 0]; output = []; score = 0; i = 0; while i < len(values): if i+1 < len(values) and values[i] == values[i+1]: append values[i]*2 to output, add that merged value to score, i += 2; else: append values[i], i += 1; after loop, pad zeros until output has length four; return output, score. No in-place pop, no scanning a zero-retaining copy, no incorrect i increments.
Runtime boundary: Main.run_demo(seed) performs a single reset, one LEFT move, prints at most one concise line, returns a dict with status, score, tiles; no input, GUI, or network.
Domain Expectations: 4x4 board with integer tiles; zeros represent empty cells.
Four directions supported: LEFT, RIGHT, UP, DOWN, mapped via Direction enum.
Merges occur from the direction of travel and each source tile merges at most once per move.
Score accumulates the sum of all merged tile values across moves.
After any move that changes the board, spawn one new tile at an empty position using deterministic RNG seeded at Game construction.
GameStatus transitions: RUNNING initially; WON when a 2048 tile appears; LOST when no moves are possible and no spawns can occur.
reset() clears board and score, spawns two initial tiles deterministically.
Pure move_line_left() obeys the exact filter-compact-merge algorithm and returns both the resulting line and the merge score.
Product Goals: Deliver correct, deterministic core 2048 mechanics with clear APIs.
Ensure maintainable, acyclic, and testable architecture aligned with Python 3.10.

User Stories: As a player, I want to move tiles in four directions and see tiles merge correctly so I can strategize to reach 2048.
As a player, I want the score to reflect merged values so I can track my performance.
As a developer, I want a deterministic seed-based RNG for reproducible tests and debugging.
As a developer, I want a pure function for line merges to facilitate unit testing independent of game state.

Requirement Analysis: We must implement a 2048 core engine with a 4x4 board, correct single-merge-per-move rules, score accumulation, deterministic seeded tile spawning, and clear win/loss/reset states. The repository must adhere strictly to the Python protocol: requirements.txt, Main.py, and tests/test_main.py as the only protocol-mandated files, with tests run via pytest. Main.py must remain a thin runtime entry exposing exactly run_demo(seed: int = 0) -> dict, using absolute imports: from twenty48.game import Game and from twenty48.types import Direction. The pure function move_line_left(line: list[int]) -> tuple[list[int], int] is canonical: it must filter zeros first using values = [v for v in line if v != 0], then merge left-to-right using the i+=2/i+=1 algorithm, pad zeros to length four, and return the new line and merge score; in-place pop or zero-retaining scans are forbidden. Tests must include the three exact fixtures—including the gap-compaction case—to prevent incorrect implementations. The architecture must separate domain logic from runtime concerns, maintain acyclic imports, and restrict Python features to 3.10-compatible APIs.
